state.customer_report: We'd like a quote to add a dedicated circuit for a hot tub on the back patio. While you're here, the kitchen lights dim whenever the microwave and toaster run at the same time, and twice last week the breaker labeled 'kitchen' tripped when both were on. Nothing smells or feels warm; we reset it and it holds until the next time.

rationale: The report contains three symptoms (a new work request, dimming, and breaker trips), and the contract's stated precedence puts breaker_trips ahead of flicker_or_dimming and new_work_request regardless of which one the customer states first or treats as the main ask.

state.condition_report: The outlet by the bathroom sink is dead. Its test button does nothing and the reset button will not stay in. No smell, no heat, and nothing else is affected.

rationale: A dead outlet with no hazard sign and no stated assessment trigger is routine.
The report is empty.

state.condition_report: Storm runoff flooded the finished basement last week to about knee height. The homeowner switched off the breaker for the basement receptacle circuit before the water rose, and it has stayed off; the panel is upstairs and stayed dry. Four wall receptacles on that circuit were under water for two days, the water has since been pumped out, and the homeowner wants to know whether the circuit can be turned back on. No shock, smell, smoke, or scorching has been noticed, and nothing on that circuit has been touched since.

rationale: The contract's hazard sign is water contact with energized equipment, and the report states the submerged receptacles were de-energized before the water rose and remain off, so no immediate-hazard sign is described; devices that were under water still require a qualified assessment before re-energizing, so needs_assessment applies rather than routine.

state.work_description: Add three new receptacles along the garage wall on a new 20-amp circuit from the existing panel.

rationale: New outlets on a new branch circuit, with no service or panel change.
The description is empty.

state.work_description: Customer's garage: the 20-amp single-pole breaker feeding the garage receptacles keeps failing to reset, so replace that breaker in the existing panel with the same make, type, and rating. Also install two new receptacles on the workbench wall, fed from that same garage circuit and extended with new cable through the finished wall. No change to the panel itself, the meter, or the service.

rationale: Replacing one breaker with an equivalent in the same panel is a component replaced like-for-like, not a change to the panel itself, while adding two receptacles on an extended run is a circuit addition or extension; the stated precedence puts circuit_addition_or_extension above like_for_like_replacement.

state.office_message: Subject: Revisions required for standby generator permit, City of Example Building Division. Before the reviewer can accept corrected plans, please upload the manufacturer's installation instructions for the transfer equipment to the permit portal. After those are received, revise sheet E-2 to show the transfer switch location and the feeder routing and resubmit the plan set. The resubmittal fee must be paid at that time before review resumes.

rationale: The subject line frames the message as a resubmittal, but the body asks first for the manufacturer's instructions to be uploaded, with the plan revision and the fee following; the contract selects the request the message asks for first.

state.product_description: Tamper-resistant, weather-resistant 20 A / 125 V duplex receptacle with built-in surge protection and a green protection-status indicator light that goes out when surge protection is no longer active. Self-grounding mounting strap, back-wire and side-wire terminals, and an optional audible alarm. Rated for use with wet-location in-use covers; nylon face in white, ivory, or gray.

rationale: Surge protection, tamper and weather resistance, a protection-status indicator, and a self-grounding strap are none of them ground-fault protection for people or arc-fault protection, so the contract's 'neither' case gives standard; the mismatch with required_type is left to code.
